basis.invariant: a stream parser must give the same result however the bytes are split into reads (raw.rs pushes one byte at a time)
basis.plan-firmware: the plan says the iGate firmware strips the prefix and ends lines with CRLF (firmware not re-read: UNVERIFIED)
basis.source-read: read in the DV-Router source (the file:line list of the scenario); not run against a binary

limits.lora_payload_max_note: informational only: the receive path has no 255 byte limit

scenarios.name: line-crlf
scenarios.note: one line, the profile's own prefix, CRLF

scenarios.name: three-lines-one-read
scenarios.note: three lines in one read

scenarios.name: three-lines-three-reads
scenarios.note: the same, one line per read

scenarios.name: unprefixed-line
scenarios.note: a line WITHOUT the prefix: what the firmware sends to the host

scenarios.name: prefixed-line
scenarios.note: a line WITH 3C FF 01: the raw radio payload

scenarios.name: mixed-prefix
scenarios.note: prefixed, plain, prefixed in one stream

scenarios.name: lf-only
scenarios.note: LF is a complete terminator (no CR)

scenarios.name: cr-only
scenarios.note: CR with no LF, then the connection closes: nothing is delivered and nothing is counted

scenarios.name: lf-only-two-lines
scenarios.note: two lines, LF only: two lines

scenarios.name: no-terminator-open
scenarios.note: a complete-looking line with no terminator, connection stays open: nothing is delivered

scenarios.name: no-terminator-eof
scenarios.note: the same, then the connection closes: the partial line is discarded, not flushed and not counted

scenarios.name: double-crlf
scenarios.note: a line then an extra CRLF: the empty line is a rejected frame (one bad frame)

scenarios.name: cr-before-text
scenarios.note: CR followed by anything but LF invalidates the line (one bad frame), the next line is fine

scenarios.name: cr-cr-lf
scenarios.note: CR CR LF: the second CR invalidates the line

scenarios.name: empty-line
scenarios.note: a single CRLF: an empty frame, one bad frame, nothing delivered

scenarios.name: empty-lines-between
scenarios.note: lines with several empty lines between: each empty line is one bad frame

scenarios.name: space-line
scenarios.note: a line of one space: framed, then refused by the TNC2 parser

scenarios.name: prefix-3cff02
scenarios.note: 3C FF 02: last byte differs

scenarios.name: prefix-3dff01
scenarios.note: 3D FF 01: first byte differs

scenarios.name: prefix-3cfe01
scenarios.note: 3C FE 01: middle byte differs

scenarios.name: prefix-swapped
scenarios.note: FF 3C 01: right bytes, wrong order

scenarios.name: prefix-two-bytes
scenarios.note: 3C FF only: the third byte is missing

scenarios.name: prefix-ascii-hex
scenarios.note: the text '3cff01' in front of the line

scenarios.name: prefix-twice
scenarios.note: 3C FF 01 3C FF 01 and the line: one prefix is removed, the second is part of the line and the TNC2 parser refuses it

scenarios.name: prefix-only
scenarios.note: 3C FF 01 and nothing else: an empty payload with the prefix configured, else a line the TNC2 parser refuses

scenarios.name: prefix-twice-then-good
scenarios.note: a doubled prefix line, then a good line: the good one still arrives

scenarios.name: junk-no-gt
scenarios.note: no '>' after the source

scenarios.name: junk-no-colon
scenarios.note: no ':' before the information

scenarios.name: junk-empty-source
scenarios.note: empty source

scenarios.name: junk-empty-dest
scenarios.note: empty destination

scenarios.name: junk-empty-digi
scenarios.note: an empty digipeater

scenarios.name: junk-text
scenarios.note: plain text

scenarios.name: junk-binary
scenarios.note: binary bytes (the header is not UTF-8)

scenarios.name: junk-nul
scenarios.note: NUL byte in the information: the framer invalidates the line (one bad frame)

scenarios.name: tnc2-lowercase
scenarios.note: lower case callsigns: refused by the TNC2 parser

scenarios.note: SSID 16: valid for the TNC2 parser (any alphanumeric suffix; AX.25 would refuse it)

scenarios.name: tnc2-call-7
scenarios.note: seven character callsign: valid for the TNC2 parser (AX.25 would refuse it)

scenarios.name: tnc2-digis-9
scenarios.note: nine digipeaters: valid for the TNC2 parser (up to 32; AX.25 would refuse it)

scenarios.name: tnc2-info-empty
scenarios.note: valid header, empty information

scenarios.name: tnc2-info-high
scenarios.note: information with UTF-8 bytes

scenarios.name: tnc2-digis-8
scenarios.note: eight digipeaters

scenarios.name: tnc2-digi-star
scenarios.note: a digipeater with the has-been-repeated star

scenarios.name: size-80
scenarios.note: an ordinary line

scenarios.name: size-255
scenarios.note: 255 bytes after the prefix (the LoRa payload size is no limit on this path)

scenarios.name: size-256
scenarios.note: 256 bytes after the prefix

scenarios.name: size-510
scenarios.note: 510 bytes after the prefix: the limit (on the wire 510 + the prefix length)

scenarios.name: size-511
scenarios.note: 511 bytes after the prefix: TooLong, one bad frame

scenarios.name: size-1024
scenarios.note: 1024 bytes

scenarios.name: size-4096
scenarios.note: 4096 bytes

scenarios.name: overlong-then-good
scenarios.note: an overlong line (1024 bytes), then a good one: the good one still arrives

scenarios.name: overlong-4096-then-good
scenarios.note: 4096 bytes, then a good line

scenarios.name: overlong-split-then-good
scenarios.note: an overlong line (2048 bytes) over three reads, then a good one

scenarios.name: overlong-no-terminator
scenarios.note: 2048 bytes and no terminator, connection open: nothing is delivered and nothing is counted yet (TooLong is reported at the next LF); the buffer is fixed, nothing grows

scenarios.name: split-mid-line
scenarios.note: a line over two reads, cut in the middle

scenarios.name: split-before-crlf
scenarios.note: the line in one read, CRLF in the next

scenarios.name: split-between-cr-lf
scenarios.note: cut between CR and LF

scenarios.name: split-after-prefix
scenarios.note: the prefix in one read, the line in the next (the empty profile cuts at 0)

scenarios.name: split-in-prefix
scenarios.note: cut after the first byte of the prefix (the empty profile cuts at 1 of the line)

scenarios.name: split-in-prefix-2
scenarios.note: cut after the second byte

scenarios.name: split-bytewise
scenarios.note: every byte its own read

scenarios.name: split-two-lines-straddle
scenarios.note: two lines, the second cut in the middle

scenarios.name: split-bad-prefix
scenarios.note: a bad prefix over two reads: still refused

scenarios.name: mid-line-connect
scenarios.note: the connection starts in the middle of a line (the tail of one), then good lines

scenarios.name: garbage-between-lines
scenarios.note: good, junk, good: the junk does not break the next line

scenarios.name: bin-valid
scenarios.note: one frame: header, prefix, AX.25 UI frame

scenarios.name: bin-two-frames-one-read
scenarios.note: two frames in one read

scenarios.name: bin-two-frames-two-reads
scenarios.note: one frame per read

scenarios.name: bin-split-header
scenarios.note: the 2-byte length header split over two reads

scenarios.name: bin-split-in-payload
scenarios.note: the frame cut in the middle of the payload (and inside the prefix for the 3cff01 profile)

scenarios.name: bin-bytewise
scenarios.note: every byte its own read

scenarios.name: bin-zero-length
scenarios.note: length 0000: invalid and TERMINAL (the adapter closes the connection); the frame behind it is never read

scenarios.name: bin-length-equals-prefix
scenarios.note: length equal to the prefix length (0 for the empty profile): no payload, terminal

scenarios.name: bin-one-byte-payload
scenarios.note: length = prefix + 1: framed, but one byte is no AX.25 frame: one bad frame, the connection stays and the next frame arrives

scenarios.name: bin-max
scenarios.note: the largest frame: 1100 bytes after the prefix (length 1100 + prefix), a valid UI frame

scenarios.name: bin-over-max
scenarios.note: 1101 bytes after the prefix: TooLong and TERMINAL (the connection is closed)

scenarios.name: bin-header-ffff
scenarios.note: length FFFF: TooLong and terminal

scenarios.name: bin-over-max-then-good
scenarios.note: a good frame first, then a too long length: the first arrives, the connection is closed, a later frame is never read

scenarios.name: bin-wrong-prefix-then-good
scenarios.note: a frame whose prefix is wrong (for the empty profile: a frame with a corrupt address): one bad frame, framing stays aligned, the next frame arrives

scenarios.name: bin-not-ax25
scenarios.note: a payload of 11 bytes: shorter than 16, no AX.25 frame: one bad frame, then a good frame

scenarios.name: bin-15-bytes
scenarios.note: 15 bytes (two addresses and a control byte, no PID): bad frame

scenarios.name: bin-16-bytes
scenarios.note: 16 bytes (two addresses, control and PID, empty information): the smallest frame

scenarios.name: bin-not-ui
scenarios.note: control byte 0x13 instead of 0x03: bad frame

scenarios.name: bin-bad-pid
scenarios.note: PID 0xCF instead of 0xF0: bad frame

scenarios.name: bin-lowercase-address
scenarios.note: a lower case letter in the destination address: bad frame

scenarios.name: bin-nine-digipeaters
scenarios.note: nine digipeaters: more than the AX.25 maximum of 8, bad frame

verdicts.accept: delivered end to end, in this order, prefix removed (the binary AX.25 frame for framing raw)
verdicts.connection_closed: the adapter closes the connection after this stream (binary terminal length)
verdicts.edge_bad_frames: increment of the edge modem counter dv_edge_modem_total{result="bad_frame"} for the whole stream (framing errors; for binary also a payload that is no AX.25 frame)
verdicts.reject: NOT delivered, the frame as received (text: the line without its terminator; binary: the bytes after the header, the two header bytes for a terminal length)
verdicts.unspecified: always empty since schema 2 (every case is decided by the source lines in `sources`)
verdicts.worker_invalid_hex: text lines the edge delivers (counted rx) that the worker's TNC2 parser refuses (dv_pkt_reject_total{reason="invalid"}); the line as the worker sees it (prefix removed)
